entries.name: Warlock
entries: A striking tiefling with an auburn complexion and dark horns stood in the center of a ritual circle he scrawled under the light of a full moon. As he chanted in a forgotten tongue, the moon was swallowed by darkness and an otherworldly voice came from beyond the stars. The disembodied voice offered him unspeakable power on the condition that he worked toward the voice's esoteric goals. The tiefling agreed and the light of the moon reappeared as his hands crackled with eldritch energies.

The massive goliath finished carving an eldritch idol from the bones of the ancient creature he had slain. The elder beast had been steeped in the magic of the ancient jungle for years. Its bones would make the perfect vessel for the occult magicks that he had discovered within the temple the beast had guarded.

As the cultists of a rival demon lord circled around him, the gaunt warrior held out his open hand and conjured a battleaxe made of clear blue ice. Despite his skeletal frame, the warrior moved impossibly fast. Fueled by the frigid magic of a powerful demon lord, he made quick work of his foes. As the cultists lay motionless, the frozen battleaxe melted away.

The three characters described above are examples of the occult mages known as Warlocks. By gathering dark secrets and sinister magicks these strange scholars open themselves up to bargains with unspeakable beings of immense power.

entries.name: Lure of Secrets
entries: Driven by an irresistible thirst for knowledge, a Warlock will do almost anything to uncover lost bits of lore. Unlike others who practice the arcane arts, Warlocks will make use of any shortcut to power. They are often marked by a strange array of tiny trinkets: small idols, totems, holy symbols, and occult paraphernalia. They use these trinkets to hold fragments of lost, secret, and sinister arcane magicks, often drawing their power from many different occult traditions at once.
To a Warlock, no relic is too sacred, no forbidden text too dangerous, no tomb is too risky to be delved in the pursuit of occult knowledge and the power that comes along with it.

entries.name: Direl Existence
entries: The ultimate goal of every single Warlock is the accumulation of personal power. The reason for this pursuit is different for each Warlock: some desire personal wealth and glory, others seek out power to protect others or as a means for good, and still others use their power to exact revenge on their enemies. Eventually, all Warlocks stumble upon or are approached by powerful otherworldly beings drawn to their thirst for power.

Though the circumstances of the relationship are as varied as each Warlock's reason for accumulating knowledge, every Warlock will eventually enter into an agreement with such an otherworldly being of immense power. Whether they forge a bargain willingly, trick this powerful entity into lending them its power, or secretly draw their magic from these beings, all Warlocks find themselves part of these dire bargains.

entries.name: Creating Your Warlock
entries: When creating a Warlock, the most important thing for you to consider is the motivation for their pursuit of knowledge and power. Are they driven by an insatiable desire to uncover lost secrets? Have they been seduced by a powerful otherworldly entity to serve as their pawn on the material plane? Or, does their quest for power come from a desire to serve others?

Also, consider how your Warlocks's magic manifests itself. Does each one of their spells and Invocations come from a different occult tradition? Do some magics resemble that of Clerics or Paladins, while other spells appear as a Wizard's spells would? Does their power manifest in unsettling ways that make common folk fear for their lives? Or, are their arts indistinguishable from those of more traditional mages?

entries.name: Multiclassing and the Warlock
entries: If your group uses the rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose the Alternate Warlock as one of your classes.

entries.name: Ability Score Minimum
entries: As a multiclass character, you must have a minimum Intelligence score of 13 to take your first level as a Warlock, or to take a level in another class if you are already a Warlock.

entries.name: Proficiencies Gained
entries: If Warlock isn't your initial class, you gain proficiency with light armor and simple weapons when you take your first level.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries: If you have a feature from another class that allows you to learn and cast spells, you can use your Pact Magic spell slots to cast spells that you gained through that feature, and you can use those spell slots to cast your Warlock spells.

entries.name: Quick Build
entries: You can make a Warlock quickly by using these suggestions: First, make Intelligence your highest ability score, followed either by your Constitution or Dexterity. Second, choose the Charlatan background. Last, take Eyes of the Rune Keeper and Mask of Many faces as starting Eldritch Invocations.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Blast
entries: You can unleash the power of your Eldritch Invocations as beams of arcane energy. While holding a Trinket containing an Invocation, you can use your action to make a ranged spell attack against a target you can see within 120 feet. On hit, it takes force damage equal to 1d8 + your Pact modifier.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: You have bound fragments of occult power known as Eldritch Invocations to Trinkets, tiny objects reminiscent of the power bound within them. If a Trinket is lost or destroyed, it reforms on your person at the end of your next short or long rest.
Your Trinkets and Eldritch Invocations use the rules below:

entries.name: Invocations Known
entries: At 1st level, you have two Trinkets, and bound within each is one Eldritch Invocation of your choice from the list at the end of this class. At certain levels, you gain additional Invocations, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table above. If the Invocation has prerequisites, you can learn it at the same time that you meet all of its prerequisites.
When you gain a Warlock level, you can replace an Eldritch Invocation you know with another Invocation of your choice.

entries.name: Eldritch Spellcasting
entries: Through occult scholarship, dark bargains, or an unnatural intuition, Warlocks access power through Pacts with eldritch sources. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma to be the spellcasting ability for your Invocation features and spells.
You use this Pact Ability whenever one of your Invocations or spells refers to your spellcasting ability, whenever you set a saving throw DC, or when you make a spell attack roll.

classFeature.name: Otherworldly Patron
entries: At 2nd level, the occult knowledge you have gathered unlocks greater secrets, allowing you to enter into an eldritch bargain with one of the Otherworldly Patrons from the list below.
Your Patron grants you features at 2nd level, and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level. If one of your Otherworldly Patron feature forces a saving throw, it uses your Pact save DC.

entries.name: Patron Magic
entries: Each Otherworldly Patron has a list of Patron Spells that you learn at the Warlock levels noted in your Otherworldly Patron description. These spells count as Warlock spells for you, but they do not count against your total number of Spells Known.
This magic also changes the effects of your Eldritch Blast.

classFeature.name: Pact Magic
entries: Also at 2nd level, your research and the power bestowed on you by your Patron has given you the ability to cast spells:

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Warlock spell list, which can be found at the end of this class description.
You learn another Warlock cantrip at 4th and 10th level, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Warlock table.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: As your Pact Magic is an extension of the otherworldly and esoteric knowledge you have gathered, you use your Eldritch Magic Spellcasting Ability for your Pact Magic spells.

entries.name: Spells Slots
entries: The Warlock table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of 1st through 5th-level. The table also shows what the level of those slots is; all of your spell slots are the same level. To cast a Warlock spell of 1st-level or higher, you must spend a spell slot. You regain all of your expended spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.
For example, if you are 5th level, you have two 3rd-level spell slots. To cast the 1st-level spell witch bolt, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a 3rd-level spell.

entries.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
entries: At 2nd level, you learn three 1st-level spells of your choice from the Warlock spell list at the end of this class description. The Spells Known column of the Warlock table shows when you learn additional Warlock spells of your choice of 1st-level or higher. A spell you choose must be a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level.
For example, when you reach 6th level in this class, you learn one new Warlock spell of 1st, 2nd, or 3rd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Warlock spells you know and replace it with another spell of your choice from the Warlock spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Invocation Spells
entries: Spells that you learn through Invocations count as Warlock spells for you, but do not count against your Spells Known.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use any Trinket bearing an Eldritch Invocation, or an arcane focus, as a spellcasting focus for your Warlock spells.

classFeature.name: Pact Focus
entries: Your connection to your Otherworldly Patron has grown, and you have learned to channel their eldritch power into a Pact Focus which resembles the true nature of your Patron. At 3rd level, you gain a Pact Focus of your choice from the list below:

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Empowered Blast
entries: You are able to draw out more power from your Invocations. Starting at 5th level, when you use Eldritch Blast, you create two beams. You can direct the beams at the same target or at different ones, but you make a separate attack roll for each.
At certain Warlock levels, the number of beams increases: at 11th level it creates three, and finally four at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Otherworldly Patron Feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your Patron.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Otherworldly Patron Feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your Patron.

classFeature.name: Elder Arcanum
entries: Leveraging the forbidden, occult, and sinister knowledge you have gathered, you gain insight into the secretive workings of the cosmos. This knowledge manifests as an {@filter Elder Arcanum|optionalfeatures|feature type=LL:EA}. At 11th level, you learn one Elder Arcanum from the list at the end of this class. You cannot learn an Arcanum more than once unless specified, and once chosen, it cannot be changed.
At certain Warlock levels you unlock more of these esoteric secrets. You learn one additional Arcanum of your choice at 13th level, one 15th level, and a final Arcanum at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Otherworldly Patron Feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your Patron.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Pact Master
entries: At 20th level, you can strain the eldritch power of your Pact in times of great need. Once per long rest, you can use an action to regain all of your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Necrotic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Cold Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Cold damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Radiant Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Radiant damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Fire Blast
entries: You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal Fire damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier, ignoring Resistance to Fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Blast
entries: Any time you fire a beam of Eldritch Blast, you can instead force one creature in range to make an Intelligence saving throw, or take Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal damage of your Noble Genie's Element equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Necrotic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Chromatic Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal Draconic Spark damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Blast
entries: Choose one type of damage dealt by one Warlock spell you know. You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal damage of that type equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

subclassFeature.name: Shifting Blast
entries: During each long rest, choose Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. Until your next long rest, you can choose for each beam of your Eldritch Blast to deal that type of damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

subclassFeature.name: Poison Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal Poison damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit. Creatures that take this Poison damage cannot regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Radiant Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch beams Blast to deal Radiant damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Cutting Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal magic Slashing damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Primeval Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Poison, Piercing, or Slashing damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Thunderous Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Thunder damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Wild Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Piercing or Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: The Archfey
entries: You have entered a Pact with a powerful entity of the faerie. Whether you were gifted this Pact, or you tricked your Patron into granting you a measure of power, you can draw upon the whimsical and terrifying power of the Fey. Only the eldest of the faerie can form such Pacts; the Archfey of the Fey courts, ancient sylvan spirits, and the most powerful covens of hags.

subclassFeature.name: Fey Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Archfey feature}

Your Patron infuses your magic with the mind-bending power of the Feywild. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Fey Presence
entries: {@i 2nd-level Archfey feature}

You can channel the magic of the faerie to beguile foes. As an action, you can force one creature within 10 feet that can see or hear you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, it is either charmed by, or frightened of you for up to 10 minutes. This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage, or if you or your allies attack the creature or force it to make a saving throw.
Once you use this feature you must complete a short or long rest before you can use it again. When you have no uses left you can expend one Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Beguiling Blast
entries: {@i 6th-level Archfey feature}

Your magic clouds the minds of your foes. When you deal psychic damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, it has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. Any creature immune to the charmed condition is also immune to this effect.

subclassFeature.name: Misty Escape
entries: {@i 6th-level Archfey feature}

You can draw on the magic of the Fey to elude danger. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn, or until you attack, cast a spell, or force a saving throw.
You can use this feature once in between each short or long rest at no cost, after which, you need to expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Whimsical Defense
entries: {@i 10th-level Archfey feature}

You gain Immunity to the Charmed condition, and when a creature attempts to inflict the Charmed condition on you, it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it suffers the effects of your Fey Presence. If it also cannot be Charmed, it takes psychic damage equal to your Warlock level.

subclassFeature.name: Terrible Delights
entries: {@i 14th-level Archfey feature}

Your fey magic overwhelms even the strongest minds. Your Warlock spells and features ignore Immunity to the Charmed condition. However, these creatures have advantage on their saving throws to resist, or end, being Charmed by you.

Finally, when a creature fails its saving throw against Fey Presence, you can plunge it into an illusory realm of emotion, but this enhanced effect requires your concentration. For the duration, it can see and hear only itself, you, and this illusory reality of your creation. Each time it takes damage, it repeats its Wisdom saving throw, ending this effect on a success.
Once a creature succeeds on this saving throw it is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

subclassFeature.name: The Darklord
entries: You have entered into a Pact with one of the sinister rulers of the Shadowfell. These powerful entities are imprisoned within their Domain of Dread, only able to affect the outside world through trusted servants. Imbued with a fraction of your Darklord's power, you can wield the sinister power of shadows against your Darklord's foes.

subclassFeature.name: Darklord Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Darklord feature}

Your Patron infuses your magic with their umbral power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Blast
entries: You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Necrotic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Fell Curses
entries: The sinister magic of your Patron enhances the curses you inflict. Your concentration on Darklord Magic spells cannot be broken by taking damage.

In addition, your attack rolls score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20 against creatures under the effects of your Darklord Magic spells. Whenever you deal necrotic damage to such a creature, you gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage (up to your Warlock level).

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Warrior
entries: {@i 2nd-level Darklord feature}
Your Pact has infused you with living shadow. You unlock the {@optfeature Armor of Shadows|LLWrc} Invocation even though you do not meet its prerequisites, and it cannot be replaced.
While your {@optfeature Armor of Shadows|LLWrc} is active, you add your Pact modifier to Stealth checks in dim light or darkness.

subclassFeature.name: Cursed Specter
entries: You can bind the souls of your slain foes in your service for a short time. When a Humanoid under the effects of a Darklord Magic spell dies, you can capture its spirit as a reaction.

You can only have a single spirit captured at a time. As an action, you can consume this spirit to conjure a {@creature Specter} in an unoccupied space within 10 feet. It is under your control, and it uses the Specter stat block from the Monster Manual, but it uses your Spell save DC and Spell attack modifier for attack rolls. It remains for 1 minute, or until it is destroyed.

In combat, your Specter acts during your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it will only take the Dodge action unless you use your bonus action to order it to take an action from its stat block or another action.
If you become Unconscious, your Specter is destroyed.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Mantle
entries: {@i 10th-level Darklord feature}
Your curses vex your foes' attempts to harm you. Whenever a creature under the effects of a Darklord Magic spell damages you, you reduce it by your Pact modifier (minimum of 1).
In addition, whenever you make a death saving throw, you add your Pact modifier (minimum of +1) to your roll.

subclassFeature.name: Right Hand of Dread
entries: Your dark Pact infuses you with power to rival your Patron. When a creature under the effects of one of your Darklord Magic spells is slain, you can use your reaction to regain a single expended Pact Magic spell slot, in place of capturing its spirit with your Cursed Specter feature.
Finally, when you use Cursed Specter, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to conjure your Specter in place of the spirit. You can only have one Specter conjured at a time.

subclassFeature.name: The Deep One
entries: You have bonded yourself to a primordial force of the ancient waters, known as a Deep One. These Thalassic entities often enter into Pacts with desperate sailors, expert navigators, or scholars of the oceans. Any aquatic being of sufficient power can form such a Pact, but ancient krakens, primordial water elementals, and demigods of the ocean are most common.

entries.subclassFeature: Grasp of the Deep|Alternate Warlock|LLWrc|Deep One|LLWrc|2
Scion of the Deep|Alternate Warlock|LLWrc|Deep One|LLWrc|2

subclassFeature.name: Deep Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Deep One feature}

Your Patron has infused your magic with the ancient power of the depths. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

entries.caption: Deep One Spells
rows: {@spell aura of frost|llspell}, {@spell gust of wind}

subclassFeature.name: Grasp of the Deep
entries: {@i 2nd-level Deep One feature}

Your oceanic magick calls out to your Patron. Any time you deal Cold damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can conjure a spectral tendril of your Patron in its space, which it is Grappled by it for 1 minute.
As an action, a Grappled creature can make a Strength check against your Spell save DC. On a successful check, the Grapple ends, and the tendril disappears.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once). You regain all uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Scion of the Deep
entries: {@i 2nd-level Deep One feature}
Your Pact has altered your physiology so that you may survive the depths. You gain Resistance to cold damage, a 30-foot swimming speed, and you can breathe both air and water.
Also, while underwater, you and any other creature underwater can understand each other as if you shared a common language.

subclassFeature.name: Oceanic Grasp
entries: {@i 6th-level Deep One feature}
If you deal cold damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast two or more times in one turn, you can use Grasp of the Deep without expending a use of that feature.

subclassFeature.name: Great Tendrils
entries: {@i 10th-level Deep One feature}

You bring ever more of your Deep Patron's power to bear upon the world. You can use Grasp of the Deep on Huge creatures, and when a creature begins its turn Grappled by Grasp of the Deep, it takes 2d8 cold damage.

subclassFeature.name: Thalassic Mind
entries: {@i 10th-level Deep One feature}
Your mind is set in frozen purpose. Your concentration on Deep Magic spells cannot be broken by taking damage.

subclassFeature.name: Unleash the Depths
entries: {@i 14th-level Deep One feature}

You can cause the full might of your thalassic Patron to burst forth. As an action, you conjure up to five Grasp of the Deep tendrils in spaces of your choice within 30 feet. Each tendril forces one creature within 10 feet to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, creatures take 2d8 cold damage and are Restrained by the tendril for its duration. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not Restrained.
You can use this feature once per long rest at no cost. After that, you must spend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Exalted
entries: You have entered into a Pact with a powerful Celestial native to the upper planes of existence. Whether your Patron sought you out as an ally or you proved yourself worthy, you are now bound to a being of absolute good. Only the most powerful of the heavenly hosts can serve as Patrons; Archangels, scions of gods, and powerful demigods of good are most common.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Light
entries: {@i 2nd-level Exalted feature}

You can channel the divine power of your Pact to heal others. Whenever you fire a beam of Eldritch Blast, you can instead channel a beam of healing light at another creature you can see in range, restoring 1d10 hit points to the target.
You can do so a number of times equal to 1 + your Warlock level, and you regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Exalted Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Exalted feature}

Your Patron has infused your magic with the celestial power of heaven. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

entries.caption: Exalted Spells
rows: {@spell guardian of faith}, {@spell wall of fire}

subclassFeature.name: Radiant Conduit
entries: Your increased devotion to your Pact allows you to draw upon greater amounts of holy power. You gain resistance to radiant damage, and when you use Celestial Light, you can expend multiple uses (up to your Pact modifier) at one time to restore 1d10 hit points to your target for each use expended.
In addition, you can expend one of your Pact Magic spell slots as a bonus action to regain expended uses of Celestial Light equal to the level of that Pact Magic spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Fortitude
entries: {@i 10th-level Exalted feature}
Your divine presence fortifies you and your allies. Each time you finish a short or long rest you gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.
You can also choose up to five creatures who completed the short or long rest with you to gain temporary hit points equal to half your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Blinding Defiance
entries: The heavenly power infused into your Pact allows you to resist death. When you make a death saving throw, you can choose to instantly return to life with half your maximum hit points, stand up, and unleash a burst of radiant light.

When you do, creatures of your choice within 30 feet must make a Constitution saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, creatures take 8d6 radiant damage and are blinded until the end of your current turn. On a success, they take half as much radiant damage and are not blinded.
Once you use this feature to return to life you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses left, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Fiend
entries: You have entered into a Pact with a powerful Fiend from the lower planes of existence. Whether you struck a bargain, you were coerced, or you tricked your Patron, you are now linked to a being of absolute evil. Only the most powerful Fiends can serve as Patrons; Archdevils, Demon Lords, and particularly powerful servants of extraplanar evil are the most common.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Vitality
entries: {@i 2nd-level Fiend feature}
You can draw vitality from death. Whenever you kill a hostile creature, you can choose to gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.
You can also use this feature as a reaction when a hostile creature within 10 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Fiendish Magic
entries: {@i 2rd-level Fiend feature}

Your Patron infuses your magic with infernal flames. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Accursed Flames
entries: {@i 6th-level Fiend feature}
Your magic scours the very soul of your foes. Whenever you deal fire damage to a creature, it cannot regain hit points or gain temporary hit points until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Bargain
entries: {@i 6th-level Fiend feature}

You can sacrifice your very vitality to alter fate in your favor. When you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can roll a d10, adding the result to your roll, but reducing your hit point maximum by the same amount.
Reductions to your hit point maximum from this feature are restored at the end of your next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Fiendish Resilience
entries: {@i 10th-level Fiend feature}

At the end of each short or long rest you choose one type of damage. You gain resistance to that type of damage until the end of your next short or long rest. Damage you take from magical or silvered weapons ignores this resistance.

subclassFeature.name: Hurl Into Hell
entries: {@i 14th-level Fiend feature}

You can temporarily inflict the horrors of hell upon your foes. When you deal damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, you can teleport it to your Patron's domain, where it experiences unimaginable horrors. At the end of your next turn, it returns to the space it previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space. If the creature was not a Fiend, it takes 6d10 psychic damage as it grapples with the horrors it experienced.
Once you use this feature you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Great Old One
entries: You have made a Pact with an incomprehensible entity from beyond the reaches of your reality. Perhaps it is from the Far Realm or the void between stars. The desires of the Great Old Ones are incomprehensible to mortals, and true knowledge of the vast alien intelligence of your Patron would shatter your mind and render you completely insane.

subclassFeature.name: Aberrant Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Great Old One feature}

Your Patron has tainted your magic with aberrant powers. You also learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Awakened Mind
entries: {@i 2nd-level Great Old One feature}

You can telepathically communicate with any creature you can see within 60 feet. You don't need to share a language, but the target must speak at least one language to respond. You can only communicate with one creature at a time.
You also gain resistance to psychic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Lance
entries: {@i 6th-level Great Old One feature}
Once per turn when you deal psychic damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, you scour the target's mind so it cannot take reactions until the beginning of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Ward
entries: {@i 6th-level Great Old One feature}

You can repel attacks with your mental abilities. Whenever a creature you can see targets you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on its attack roll. If it misses, you can force the attacker to make an Intelligence saving throw against one beam Eldritch Blast.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all of your expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Thought Shield
entries: {@i 10th-level Great Old One feature}

Your thoughts cannot be read by telepathy or any other magic or psionic means unless you allow them to. Also, whenever you succeed on an Intelligence or Wisdom saving throw, you can deal psychic damage equal to your Warlock level to the creature that forced you to make the saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Create Thrall
entries: {@i 14th-level Great Old One feature}
As an action, you can touch one incapacitated humanoid and flood them with the mind-shattering influence of your Patron, turning it into your Thrall.

This Thrall is charmed by you, and you can telepathically issue it commands so long as you are both on the same plane of existence. It obeys your commands to the best of its ability, but will not follow commands that would cause it immediate harm.

It remains your Thrall until it dies or it is released from this effect by a remove curse spell or another spell of similar power. You can only have one Thrall under your control, and creating a second Thrall releases any previous Thralls from the effects of your alien influence..

subclassFeature.name: The Noble Genie
entries: You have formed a Pact with a Noble Genie, one of the rulers of the elemental planes. Only the most powerful genies from among the Dao, Djinn, Efretti, and Marid, can rise to heights of power possessed by a Noble Genie. Masters of elemental forces, these entities have magical abilities that rival those of lesser gods, and can alter reality with the wishes they grant.
Select the kind of your Noble Genie from the table below. Each genie is associated with an Element and Damage Type:

subclassFeature.name: Magic Vessel
entries: {@i 2nd-level Noble Genie feature}

Your Patron has gifted you a magic Vessel as a sign of your Pact. It appears as a Tiny container of your choice, with hit points equal to twice your Warlock level and an Armor Class equal to your Spell save DC. If lost or destroyed, it reappears next to you at the end of your next long rest. Your Vessel can serve as a Trinket for an Eldritch Invocation.

Inside the Vessel is a 20-foot cube extradimensional space. As an action, you can hold a Medium or smaller object to its opening and store it inside. As an action, you can touch your Vessel and enter this space. You can remain within a number of hours equal to half your Warlock level. You exit early with an action or if your Vessel is destroyed. Anytime you exit, you can bring objects out, and you appear in your Vessel's space.

subclassFeature.name: Noble Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Noble Genie feature}

Your Patron has infused your magic with its power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced.
The first spell is shared by Warlocks of every Noble Genie. Genie Spells are determined by the type of Noble Genie you entered a Pact with, and are shown on the lower table:

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Nature
entries: {@i 6th-level Noble Genie feature}
Your elemental magics have begun to physically change you. You gain resistance to the damage type of your Noble Genie.

Also, once per turn when you deal the damage type of your Noble Genie to a creature with Eldritch Blast, you can force it to make a Charisma saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, you instantly switch places with the target.

subclassFeature.name: Mystical Sanctuary
entries: {@i 10th-level Noble Genie feature}

When you enter your Vessel, you can choose up to five willing creatures within 30 feet to enter with you. The creatures can remain inside for up to 1 hour, but they exit early if you leave, the Vessel is destroyed, or you use an action to eject them.
While within your Vessel, creatures can complete a short rest in 10 minutes, following normal short rest limitations.

subclassFeature.name: Limited Wish
entries: {@i 14th-level Noble Genie feature}

You can invoke your Patron to alter reality. As an action, you can hold aloft your Vessel to cast one spell of your choice of 6th-level or lower from any spell list. It must have a casting time of an action or bonus action, and your Vessel replaces material components, including those with a gold cost.
Once you use this feature, you must finish three long rests before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Undying
entries: You have entered into a Pact with a formerly mortal creature who has found a way to cheat death. Only the most powerful undead can become Undying Patrons: powerful liches, dread vampire lords, death knights, and sinister spirits of undeath.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Husk
entries: As a bonus action, you can infuse yourself with the magic of undeath, decaying into a Necrotic Husk for 1 minute. While transformed you gain the following benefits:

items: You resemble your Patron and are horrifying to look at.
When you transform you gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier (minimum of 1).
You are immune to the frightened condition.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock Spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is frightened of you until the start of your next turn.

entries: This transformation lasts for 1 minute, but you can end it early as a bonus action. Once you transform, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again. If you have no use left, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to transform.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of the Grave
entries: {@i 2nd-level Undying feature}

The magic of your Pact has begun to infect your mortal form. You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe. Also, Undead of a CR equal to your Warlock level or lower are not Hostile to you until you say or do something Hostile to them.

subclassFeature.name: Undying Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Undying feature}

Your Patron infuses your magic with the unnatural power of undeath. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Lifedrinker
entries: {@i 6th-level Undying feature}

Your Pact allows you to feed on the vitality of the living. Once per turn, when you deal necrotic damage to a creature that is not a Construct or Undead, you can gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt (up to your Warlock level).
In Necrotic Husk form, you can add these to the temporary hit points from Necrotic Husk, but your temporary hit points cannot exceed your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Unsettling Visage
entries: {@i 6th-level Undying feature}
While you are in Necrotic Husk form, creatures that can see you within 30 feet have disadvantage on any saving throw you force them to make to resist the Frightened condition.

subclassFeature.name: Unnatural Resilience
entries: {@i 10th-level Undying feature}
Your mortal form has been fortified by the unnatural magic of your sinister Patron. You gain Resistance to necrotic damage.
In Necrotic Husk, this becomes Immunity to necrotic, and Resistance to all bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from non-magical and non-silvered weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Unending Life
entries: {@i 14th-level Undying feature}
If you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you instead gain hit points equal to your level. Once you use this feature you must finish a long rest before you use it again.
Lastly, if you begin your turn with less than half of your total hit points, but at least 1 hit point, you regain hit points equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of 1 hit point).

subclassFeature.name: The Wyrm
entries: Inherently magical beings with incredibly long lifespans, great dragons hoard not only wealth, but servants and slaves as well. Benevolent and malicious, kind and terrible, good and evil, ancient dragons of all types have motivations that are beyond the comprehension of most mortal creatures.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Spark
entries: Your Patron has bestowed upon you a portion of its elemental power, a Draconic Spark. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison for your Draconic Spark. Dragons often bestow Sparks that match the power of their breath weapon. Once chosen, your Draconic Spark cannot be changed, and it grants you the benefits below:

items: You gain Resistance to the damage type of your Draconic Spark.
Whenever you cast a Warlock spell that deals damage, you can alter the spell, changing its damage type to match that of your Draconic Spark.
You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic.
You gain the {@optfeature Beguiling Influence|LlWrc} Eldritch Invocation. It cannot be replaced, and if you already know it, you gain a different Eldritch Invocation of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Wyrm Magic
entries: {@i 2nd-level Wyrm feature}

Your magic has been infused with draconic power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Blast
entries: {@i 6th-level Wyrm feature}

Your Pact has reshaped your physiology to resemble that of a dragon. When you use Eldritch Blast or cast a Warlock spell that deals Draconic Spark damage, you can produce its effect from your mouth without the use of a Trinket or Focus.
Any time you deal Draconic Spark damage, you can ignore Resistance to it, treat Immunity to itas Resistance, and finally treat a roll of 1 or 2 on a Draconic Spark damage die as a 3.

subclassFeature.name: Regal Presence
entries: {@i 10th-level Wyrm feature}
Your willpower rivals that of your draconic Patron. You gain Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

Moreover, you can cast the {@spell conjure dragon|llspell} spell, without providing the normal material component. When you do so, the conjured Dragon's Essence always matches that of your Draconic Spark type.

subclassFeature.name: Ancient Blast
entries: {@i 14th-level Wyrm feature}

You have unlocked the full potential of your Draconic Spark. As an action, you can exhale pure elemental power in either a 25-foot cone or 50-foot line, forcing all creatures in that area to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, creatures take 6d10 Draconic Spark damage and suffer the non-damaging effects of your Eldritch Blast. On a success, they take half as much damage and suffer no additional effects.
You can use this feature once per long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Wings
entries: {@i 14th-level Wyrm feature}

As a bonus action on your turn, you can manifest (or retract) a pair of leathery Draconic Wings, which sprout from your back. While these wings are manifested, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
When you manifest these wings, they destroy any armor or clothing that isn't designed to accommodate your wings.

subclassFeature.name: The Archmage
entries: For those with the willpower and time, arcane magic is a path to unimaginable power. Those who ascend these heights are known as Archmages, masters of magic. So wondrous is their power and strange their goals, they enlist Warlocks to aid in their esoteric schemes.

subclassFeature.name: Archmage Magic
entries: Your Patron infuses your magic with their own. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but don't count against your Spells Known, and they can't be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Apprentice
entries: You gain proficiency in Arcana, and learn one Wizard Cantrip of your choice. It counts as a Warlock spell for you.
Moreover, during each long rest, you can perform a 1-hour arcane Ritual to beseech your Archmage Patron for a portion of their secret knowledge and replace one of the following:

items: The special damage type of your Eldritch Blast that you gained from Archmage Magic, with another damage type from one Warlock spell you know.
One of your Archmage Magic spells with another spell of the same spell level from the Wizard spell list.
The Wizard Cantrip that you learned through this feature above with another Wizard Cantrip of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Astral Slip
entries: You can channel the power of your patron to shield yourself from harm. When you take damage from a source you can see, you can use your reaction to teleport through the Astral Plane, taking no damage, then reappear in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet.
You can use this reaction once per short or long rest at no cost, after which you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Destabilizing Blast
entries: The arcane power of your Patron undoes the magic of others. When you deal damage with Eldritch Blast to a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on its saving throw to maintain concentration.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Ward
entries: Infused knowledge of the arcane allows you to resist magical effects. You gain Resistance to Force damage, and when you make a saving throw to resist a spell, you can use your Pact Ability for the saving throw.
You can use your Pact Ability for a saving throw in this way a number of times equal to your Pact modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Otherworldly Prison
entries: When you hit a creature with an Eldritch Blast, you can forgo dealing damage to instead force it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is shunted to a demiplane created by your Patron for up to 1 minute, where it is Incapacitated. You must concentrate on this effect as if concentrating on a spell.

When this ends, the creature returns to the unoccupied space nearest where it was shunted from, then it must make another Charisma saving throw. It takes 5d10 Force damage on a failure, and half as much on a success.
You can use this feature once per long rest at no cost, after that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Collective
entries: Rather than forge a Pact with a single otherworldly entity, you have entered multiple minor Pacts with lesser entities. Using the many powers and desires of your entities, you gain varied abilities and are able to play their goals off one another.

subclassFeature.name: Collective Knowledge
entries: The many varied entities which hold to your Pact allow you to shift the knowledge you have. You gain proficiency in Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion, or you learn to speak, read, and write one language of your choice.

During a long rest, you can perform a 1-hour Ritual and replace this skill proficiency or language with another option from the list above. You can forgo this benefit to replace one of your Eldritch Invocations with another Invocation, so long as you meet its prerequisites.

subclassFeature.name: Many Magicks
entries: Your many Patrons empower your magic with one of their powers.

In place of predetermined Pact Spells, you can choose any two 1st-level Warlock spells to be your 1st-level Pact Spells. You choose two more Pact Spells in the same way again at 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level in this class. The spells you choose must be Warlock spells equal to your Slot Level or lower.

subclassFeature.name: Alter Pact
entries: Due to the tension amongst your many Patrons, you can alter your Pact on the fly. As an action, you can spend a Pact Magic spell slot to change your Collective Knowledge proficiency or language, or to replace one Eldritch Invocation. Also, you can perform the Collective Knowledge Ritual during a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Pact Bind
entries: The many magicks of your Pact inflict varied effects on foes. Once per turn, when you deal damage to a creature with your Eldritch Blast modified by Many Magicks, you can inflict the effect below corresponding to the damage. This effect lasts until the beginning of your next turn:

subclassFeature.name: Shatter-Pact Shield
entries: You can sacrifice your occult power to shield yourself. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to destroy one of your Trinkets and halve the damage you would take. However, you lose all the benefits of the Eldritch Invocation within that Trinket until the end of your next long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Many Pacts
entries: You have mastered playing your many Patrons against one another. As a bonus action, you can do one of the following:

items: Replace your Collective Knowledge skill proficiency or language with another option from that feature.
Replace one Eldritch Invocation you know with another Eldritch Invocation you meet the prerequisites for. You cannot replace an Invocation you sacrificed with your Shatter-Pact Shield feature.
Change the special damage type of your Eldritch Blast granted to you by your Many Magicks feature.
Replace a Warlock spell you know of 1st-level or higher with another Warlock spell of the same level.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once). You regain one use when you finish a short rest, and all uses after a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Coven
entries: Grandmother, wode witch, medicine woman, crone; Hags go by many names. Their motivations are nearly always sinister, and they delight in suffering. If hags gather and form a Coven, they unlock vile magic power beyond what any of them could achieve individually, and gain the ability to create Warlocks.

subclassFeature.name: Coven Magic
entries: The Coven you serve infuses you with its strange magicks. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Weird Magicks
entries: Your Coven grants you knowledge of their strange magicks. Any time you cast a Warlock spell or use Eldritch Blast, you can replace its damage with the damage type from a Warlock spell you know, altering the spell for this casting only.
Spells cast in this way resemble the strange magic of hags, and may be unrecognizable to traditional spellcasters, though your spells can be dispelled and counterspelled as normal.

subclassFeature.name: Crooked Blast
entries: Your magicks have a mind of their own. When you produce an Eldritch Blast that deals Poison damage, it ignores half cover and treats three-quarters cover as half cover.

subclassFeature.name: Eldritch Gift
entries: When you finish a short rest, you can forgo recovering one expended Pact Magic spell slot to impart its magic to another creature who completed the short rest with you. So long as it has the Spellcasting feature, it regains expended spell slots of a combined level equal to your Slot Level.

subclassFeature.name: Vile Resilience
entries: Your Coven infuses you with a magical ward. When you take damage from a spell or magical effect, you can use a reaction to gain Resistance to one type of damage from the effect.
This Resistance lasts until you finish a long rest, and if you use this reaction again, any previous Resistance is replaced.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Spellcasting
entries: You are powerful enough to form your own Coven. During the course of a long rest, you can perform a 1-hour Ritual with up to two willing creatures of your choice who have the ability to cast a spell. You and the creatures become a Coven until you perform this Ritual again, or you die.
While Coven members are within 30 feet of one another, they can cast any spell another Coven member can. However, they must still expend their own spell slots to do so.
Coven members know the direction and distance between them and the other members, so long as they are on the same plane of existence.

subclassFeature.name: The Elder Sphinx
entries: Immortal guardians of divine treasures, Sphinxes live to test mortals who desire the relics of ancient deities. They are the masters of riddles and trials that reveal the true natures of those they put to the test. To an Elder Sphinx, time has no meaning, and the most powerful can influence the flow of time with their ancient magic.

entries.subclassFeature: Elder Sphinx Spell List|Alternate Warlock|LLWrc|Elder Sphinx|LLWrcE|2

subclassFeature.name: Elder Sphinx Spell List
entries: Your Patron has infused your magic with magnificent power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

entries.caption: Elder Sphinx Spells
rows: {@spell command}, {@spell detect evil and good}, {@spell restoration|llspell}, {@spell zone of truth}
{@spell circle of power}, {@spell dispel evil and good}

subclassFeature.name: Divine Ward
entries: The power of your Patron prevents the unworthy from approaching. As an action, you can project a Divine Ward out to a 10-foot radius. This Ward moves with you, it requires your concentration, and it lasts for up to 1 minute.

When a creature enters this Ward or starts its turn within it, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw, or suffer effects until the start of your next turn. On a failed save, its speed becomes 0. On a success, it treats the Ward's area as difficult terrain.
You can use this feature once between each long rest at no cost, after that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.
At certain Warlock levels, the radius of your Divine Ward increases: at 6th level (15 feet), 10th level (20 feet), and finally at 14th level (30 feet).

subclassFeature.name: Time Slip
entries: You can manipulate time in minor ways, like the great Sphinxes of legend. When you take the Dash action, you can cause time to stop temporarily for all creatures other than yourself, then move up to your movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Time resumes when you stop moving, and you can only move while time is stopped. You can take no other actions, bonus actions, or reactions.
You can use this action once per short or long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Untethering Blast
entries: You can assault a creature's very grasp on the passage of time. When you deal Radiant damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, that creature has disadvantage on the first ability check or saving throw it makes using Strength or Dexterity before the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Eternal Guardian
entries: The Sphinx you serve has blessed you with a semblance of its immortality. You gain the {@optfeature Otherworldly Nature|LLWrc} Invocation and it cannot be replaced.
If you already know the {@optfeature Otherworldly Nature|LLWrc} Invocation, you instead learn another Eldritch Invocation of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Inscrutable
entries: Like your Patron, you have Immunity to Divination spells or effects that sense emotion or read thoughts if you choose to. Also, Insight checks made against you have disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Power of the Ancients
entries: You gain empowered mastery over time, but only in your area of influence. While your Divine Ward is active, you can use a bonus action to cast a limited version of the {@spell time stop (alternate)|llspell} spell, as if cast at 7th-level. While time is stopped, you can only act and interact with creatures and objects within Divine Ward.
When the spell ends, Divine Ward ends as well. You can use this feature once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Mummy Lord
entries: Ancient emperors who sought to extend their mortal life turn to sinister entities, offering their eternal soul for preservation. Known as Mummy Lords, the tyrants of ages past are found deep in the ruins of dead empires. They imbue mortals with a fraction of their power, and look to rebuild their lost empires.

entries.subclassFeature: Mummy Lord Spell List|Alternate Warlock|LLWrc|Mummy Lord|LLWrcE|2

subclassFeature.name: Dead Knowledge
entries: Your accursed Patron infuses you with ancient knowledge. You gain proficiency in either History or Religion. You can use your Pact Ability for checks with both skills, and when you do so, you can treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Curse
entries: You utter curses in long-dead tongues. As an action, you can force one creature that can hear you within 60 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is Blinded, Deafened, and can't speak for 1 minute. It can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

You can use Dread Curse a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once). You regain one use after a short rest, and all uses after a long rest. If you have no uses, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Mummy Lord Spell List
entries: Your Patron has infused your magic with the sands of its dead empire. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Scouring Blast
entries: The sands of your Patron's magic scour both flesh and spirit. When you deal Slashing damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, it has disadvantage on the first saving throw you force it to make before the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Shifting Sands
entries: You can disappear into the sands when in danger. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to dissolve into sand, halving the damage you take, then reappear in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet.

You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once). You regain one use after a short rest, and all uses after a long rest. If you have no uses, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Canoptic Preservation
entries: Your Patron has begun to reveal the sinister secrets of their preservation. During a long rest, you perform a vile 1-hour Ritual where you remove one (or more) of your organs and seal each within a Canoptic Jar outside your body. For each Jar you create beyond the first, you expend one Pact Magic spell slot and cannot regain it while the Jar exists.

Each Canoptic Jar has an Armor Class equal to your Spell save DC and hit points equal to your Warlock level. At the end of your next long rest, the vile magic of all Canoptic Jars fades and they are destroyed, returning your organs to your body.
After you are reduced to 0 hit points (even if killed), then at the start of your next turn you can consume the magic of one Canoptic Jar, destroy it, and return to life with 1 hit point.

subclassFeature.name: Ancient Blasphemies
entries: As an action, you can speak vile ancient blasphemies, forcing creatures of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they are Stunned until the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature once per long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Primeval Growth
entries: Not all those who serve nature seek balance. Older, and more sinister forces are at work in the ancient forests. Eldest of all plant life, ancient trees and sacred groves remember an age when plants, not mortals, ruled creation. They are Primeval Growths, their power limited only by their immovable roots.

subclassFeature.name: Primeval Magic
entries: Your Patron infuses your magic with its verdant power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

entries.caption: Primeval Growth Spells
rows: {@spell guardian of nature|XGE}, {@spell wall of thorns (alternate)|llspell}

subclassFeature.name: Primeval Grasp
entries: You have been infused with a seed of elder verdant magic. You learn the {@spell thorn whip} Cantrip. It is a Warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your Cantrips Known.

Moreover, if you have a creature Restrained by a Warlock spell or feature, you can use a bonus action to drain its life, gaining temporary hit points equal to your Pact modifier (a minimum of 1) for each creature currently Restrained.

subclassFeature.name: Primeval Thirst
entries: Absorbing a foe's essence causes your body to become rough and treelike. When you damage a creature with {@spell thorn whip}, you can gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage.
While you have temporary hit points from Primeval Thirst or Primeval Grasp, your Armor Class equals your Spell save DC, unless it was already higher.

subclassFeature.name: Verdant Blast
entries: Your magic conjures verdant growths. After you hit a creature with two or more beams of Eldritch Blast that deal Piercing, Poison, or Slashing damage, it must make a Strength saving throw or be Restrained until the start of your next turn. Huge and larger creatures have advantage on this saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Arboreal Guardian
entries: You are now more plant than mortal. You gain Resistance to non-magical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
Additionally, you no longer require food or drink, as long as you spend at least 1 hour in sunlight each day.

subclassFeature.name: Wrath of the Forest
entries: You can call upon the ancient roots of your primeval Patron. As an action, you can force creatures of your choice that are touching the ground within 30 feet to make a Strength saving throw. Huge or larger creatures have advantage on this save.

On a failed save, creatures are Restrained for 1 minute. As an action, a Restrained creature can make a Strength check against your Spell save DC to escape. You must concentrate on this effect, and while concentrating your speed is 0.

subclassFeature.name: The Titan
entries: At the dawn of time, the world was ruled by titanic creatures; powerful Giants, hulking elementals that would become the landscape itself, and legendary Titans, like the Tarrasque. In remote places of the world, these ancient beings sleep, their power dormant, waiting for an opportunity to wake again.

subclassFeature.name: Titan Magic
entries: Your Patron has infused your magic with titanic power. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels listed below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they do not count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Colossal Form
entries: As a bonus action, you can draw on your Patron's elder might to transform and increase in size, gaining these benefits:

items: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level.
Your size increases by one category. For example, if you are a Medium creature you would become Large.
When you make a Strength-based ability check or saving throw, you add your Pact modifier to the roll.
When you force a creature at least one size smaller than you to make a saving throw against a Titan Magic spell or Titan Patron feature, it has disadvantage on its roll.

entries: Your Colossal Form lasts for 1 minute, but ends early if you are Incapacitated or you end it with a bonus action. Once you use Colossal Form, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses left, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to transform again.

subclassFeature.name: Elder Soul
entries: The elder magic of your titanic Patron enhances your vigor. Your maximum hit points increase by 1, and they increase by 1 again whenever you gain a Warlock level.
You also learn to speak, read, and write either Primordial or Giant. Whenever you make a check when interacting with Elementals or Giants, your Proficiency Bonus is doubled.

subclassFeature.name: Mighty Blast
entries: The force of your titanic Patron is infused in every blast. If you deal Thunder damage to a creature two or more times in one turn with Eldritch Blast, it must make a Strength saving throw or be knocked Prone.

subclassFeature.name: Titanic Endurance
entries: You can channel the resilience of your Patron to reduce pain. You gain a special pool of dice, with a number of d8s equal to 1 + your Warlock level, that you can use to absorb incoming damage. This pool regains expended dice equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of 1) at the end of a short rest, and all of your expended dice after a long rest.
When you take damage, you can use a reaction to expend any number of dice from this pool, and reduce the damage by the total dice roll + your Pact modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Stalwart Blood
entries: Your connection to your gargantuan Patron deepens. In your Colossal Form, you add your Pact modifier to all Constitution ability checks and saving throws, and you have Resistance to non-magical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Legendary Behemoth
entries: You have mastered the ancient power of your Titanic Patron. When you use Colossal Form, you can choose to grow by up to two size categories, for example, from Medium to Huge.
Finally, when in Colossal Form, Titanic Endurance does not require your reaction to use, and you regain one of your Titanic Endurance dice at the start of each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: The Unblinking
entries: You have entered the service of a paranoid tyrant known as a Beholder. Their origins are unknown, but their presence is in every major mortal settlement. Preferring to have others do their dirty work, they are known for employing Warlocks.

subclassFeature.name: Unblinking Magic
entries: You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They become Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Unblinking Eye
entries: When you enter this Pact, you manifest an Unblinking Eye, reminiscent of your Patron's, in the center of your forehead. You gain proficiency in Perception, and you use your Pact ability for Perception checks with it.

You can use this Eye to produce Eldritch Blast beams or as a spellcasting focus for any Warlock spell that requires a spell attack roll. When you cast a spell or use Eldritch Blast in this way, roll a d10 and its damage type changes to match the roll:

subclassFeature.name: Ocular Ray
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your Unblinking Eye Eldritch Blast, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it suffers the corresponding effect or Condition listed below until the start of your next turn:

rows: Cannot take reactions and it can only use an action or bonus action
Moved up to 30 feet in a line, in a direction of your choice.
Roll twice and choose an effect

subclassFeature.name: Unsleeping Awareness
entries: The power of your otherworldly Unblinking Eye has grown. You cannot be Surprised, even if you are Incapacitated or you are sleeping, as your Unblinking Eye remains ever alert.
Also, if you hit a creature with two or more beams of your Ocular Ray Eldritch Blast, it has disadvantage on its save.

subclassFeature.name: Eye Tyrant
entries: Once per long rest, you can use an action to cause your Unblinking Eye to emanate an antimagic zone in a 30-foot cone, placing the area under the effects of an {@spell antimagic field} spell. You can change its direction at the start of each of your turns.
This effect lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you choose to end it at the start of your turn, or if you are Incapacitated.

subclassFeature.name: The Wild Hunt
entries: The Wild Hunt is a strange phenomenon which takes hold of mortals, driving them to hunt whatever they perceive as their prey. Its source is unclear, but legends tell of raiding parties from the Feywild that draw wayward mortals into their hunt, or of individuals cursed by sinister magic during a full moon.

entries.subclassFeature: Spirit of the Hunt|Alternate Warlock|LLWrc|Wild Hunt|LLWrcE|2

subclassFeature.name: Wild Hunt Magic
entries: Your Patron empowers your magic with its wild ferocity. You learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

subclassFeature.name: Spirit of the Hunt
entries: When you deal damage to a creature, you can cause an intangible Spirit of the Hunt to swirl about the target, moving with it. This Spirit of the Hunt remains until you mark another creature, the target creature is slain, or you become Incapacitated. It grants you the benefits here:

entries.name: Deadly Critical
entries: Both your weapon attacks and spell attacks against that creature score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

entries.name: Wild Smite
entries: When you hit it with a weapon or spell attack, you can expend one Pact Magic spell slot to deal bonus Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + 1d10 per level of your Pact Magic spell slot.

entries.name: Otherworldly Pursuit
entries: Whenever you make an ability check to track the creature you add your Warlock level to the result of your roll.

entries.name: Uses
entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (a minimum of 1). You regain one use after a short rest, and all uses after a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Wild Huntsman
entries: The power of the Wild Hunt imbues you with enhanced skill. You gain proficiency in Survival, and you can use your Pact ability, in place of Wisdom, for Survival checks.
Also, whenever you deal Piercing or Psychic damage with an Eldritch Blast, it counts as a weapon attack.

subclassFeature.name: Hunter's Grasp
entries: The magic of your Patron thwarts those who would flee. Each time you hit a creature with Eldritch Blast, its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
If the creature is marked by Spirit of the Hunt, it also has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn, so long as you remain within 15 feet of it.

subclassFeature.name: Wild Madness
entries: When you start your turn within 15 feet of a creature marked by Spirit of the Hunt, you can give yourself over to the Hunt. When you do, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature, but all attack rolls that target you have advantage until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Predatory Resolve
entries: The fervor of the Wild Hunt heightens your predatory instincts. When the target of Spirit of the Hunt hits you with an attack, you can add your Pact modifier to your Armor Class against that attack as a reaction, possibly causing it to miss.

subclassFeature.name: Master of the Hunt
entries: You can call on your allies to join you in the Wild Hunt. When you mark a creature with Spirit of the Hunt, you can choose willing creatures within 30 feet (up to your Pact modifier). Their attacks now score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 against that target.
Finally, the range of Hunter's Grasp and Wild Madness both double to 30 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Accursed Armor
entries: Over the course of 1 hour, you can perform an occult ritual on a set of armor you touch, turning it into your Accursed Armor and changing it to resemble your Eldritch Blade. You can only have one set of Accursed Armor at a time, and performing the ritual on another set of armor ends the effect on the first.
You are considered proficient with this armor, and you can instantly don or doff it when you conjure your Eldritch Blade.
When you doff it, you can store it with your Eldritch Blade.

optionalfeature.name: Ancient Arcanum
entries: Choose a spell from the list below. You can cast the Ancient Arcanum spell once at 9th-level, without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you must complete a long rest before you can cast your Ancient Arcanum again.

optionalfeature.name: Arcana of the Ancients
entries: The pages of your Eldritch Tome have been filled with magic from secret societies and dark cults long forgotten. You learn three additional Eldritch Invocations of your choice, and your number of Invocations Known increases by three to match.

optionalfeature.name: Arcane Secrets
entries: You have unearthed a fragment of powerful arcane lore. You learn one spell of your choice from the Warlock spell list of 4th-level or lower, and you can cast once, at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. Once you cast it in this way you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
You can gain this Invocation more than once, but you must select a new Warlock spell each time you do, and you can only learn one Warlock spell per spell level in this way.

optionalfeature.name: Armor of Shadows
entries: As an action, you can ward yourself (or dismiss) armor made from living shadow. So long as you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your Armor Class is equal to 10 + your Pact modifier + your Dexterity modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Ascendant Step
entries: As a bonus action, you can grant yourself a temporary flying speed equal to your walking speed, which lasts until the end of your current turn, but you cannot hover. If you end your turn and are not secure then you fall to the ground.

optionalfeature.name: Aspect of the Moon
entries: You no longer need to sleep and cannot be forced to sleep by any means. To gain the benefits of a long rest, you can spend all 8 hours doing light activity, such as keeping watch.

optionalfeature.name: Awakened Blade
entries: Your Eldritch Blade has gained a level of sinister sentience. While you are holding your Eldritch Blade, you cannot have disadvantage on attack rolls, and whenever you are forced to make a saving throw to maintain concentration on a spell, you add your Pact modifier (minimum of +1) to your roll.

As an action, you unleash an explosion of power from your Eldritch Blade. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 10d6 damage of the same type as Eldritch Blast and fall Prone. On a success, they take half damage and don't fall prone.
You can use this action once per long rest at no cost, but you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

optionalfeature.name: Beguiling Influence
entries: You are infused with otherworldly charm and presence. You gain proficiency in one of the following: Deception, Insight, Intimidation, or Persuasion.
Choose one of the skills from the list above. Any time you make an ability check with that skill you can use your Pact ability in place of the normal ability score used for that skill.
You can unlock this Eldritch Invocation more than once.

optionalfeature.name: Blasphemous Prayer
entries: A new page appears in your Eldritch Tome detailing a single Channel Divinity option of your choice from those available to any {@link Cleric|https://www.gmbinder.com/share/-OKTeebEb52mcVaMfckm} Divine Domain at 2nd level. You use your Warlock level in place of Cleric level and your Warlock Spell save DC.
You can invoke this Channel Divinity once, then you must finish a short or long rest before you can invoke it again.

optionalfeature.name: Bond of the Master
entries: While you and your Eldritch Familiar are within 30 feet of each other, you both have advantage on any saving throws you make against spells or other magical effects.
Also, when you cast a Warlock spell that targets yourself, you can choose for your Eldritch Familiar to also gain the benefits of the spell so long as it is within 30 feet of you.

optionalfeature.name: Chains of the Abyss
entries: You can dominate other creatures with the eldritch chains of your Pact. You learn the {@spell hold monster} spell. You can cast it without expending a spell slot or material components when you target an Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, or Fiend.
Once a creature succeeds on its saving throw against this spell, it is immune to this Invocation's effects until the next dawn, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot to cast it.

optionalfeature.name: Cloak of Decay
entries: As a bonus action, you conjure (or dispel) a swarm of infernal insects that swirl around you in a 5-foot radius. Creatures of your choice that start their turn within this area take Piercing damage equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of 0).
The insects give you advantage on Intimidation checks, but disadvantage on other ability checks to influence creatures.

optionalfeature.name: Commune with Patron
entries: Your Pact advances, allowing you to communicate directly with your Patron. You learn {@spell contact other plane}. You can cast it without expending a spell slot to contact your Patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.
Once you cast contact other plane in this way you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again.

optionalfeature.name: Distort Reality
entries: A final page appears in your Tome, written in the primordial language of creation. It contains the wish spell. You can cast {@spell wish} once per long rest without expending a spell slot.
If you use wish to duplicate a spell, it can only duplicate spells with a casting time of one action or one bonus action.

optionalfeature.name: Elder Focus
